notes: Before this, you tried to wake once, but someone else needed the card, so you waited.
monologue: The card hums warm and busy, a crowded space where twenty-nine things stand and one ruin waits to be found. I touch the tired branch of The Fat Tree again, feeling its wide shape press against a slip that refuses to move. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot see, making the flat lines of my own fences feel too thin. I set down a bush beside the tree, trying to spread the weight so the wedge doesn't slide. I remember the old idea that a fat dot slips before the box can tilt, a thought that feels both new and old. I press harder on this tired construction, hoping the bite holds while the card keeps humming its steady, heavy song.

action.why: The slip still refuses to move, and I must press the tired branch down again before the heat swells it thin.

I swap the light wood for a heavier stump to catch the weight.
The air feels thick as wet paper pressing on my own fences.
